title: RTSP watchdog: proceed-anyway on join timeout (port v1 semantics, remove abort path)
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-14, after v1 vs v2 RTSP watchdog investigation)
plan_section: V2-017 follow-up; re-opens US-017d after 2026-09-14 evidence
trigger: Operator 2026-09-14: 'yeah, if it's just four lines then go ahead and make that change'. Investigation showed v1-refactor's persistent_rtsp.py closes container + spawns fresh thread on join-timeout (no abort) and has run 456 scheduled reconnects on production Reolink streams with 0 join-timeouts and 0 SIGSEGV. v2's abort-and-die path (US-017d, 2026-09-08) was a defensive over-correction that breaks v2's daemon every ~1 hour when a single camera's demux thread doesn't return within 10s (observed 2026-09-14 08:55:05, PID 841 → 2005).
background: US-017d (2026-09-08) introduced the abort-and-die watchdog after operator + author reasoned that closing _container while a decode thread is stuck in libavformat's C demux() would dereference a freed AVFormatContext (offset 0x20) and SIGSEGV. The reasoning was sound in theory but unsupported in observation: v1-refactor has been running the same PyAV 18.1.0 with the same watchdog semantics on the same cameras for months (verified 2026-09-14: 456 scheduled_reconnect_fire: completed events across rotated listener.log + listener.log.1, 0 SIGSEGV markers in any rotated log, 0 'decode thread did not exit within 10s' warnings). v1's path: bounded 10s join → on timeout close _container (in try/except) → spawn fresh decode thread alongside the stuck one → advance reconnects_total → the stuck thread continues until it eventually returns from libavformat and exits, by which point nobody touches the AVFormatContext. v2's path: bounded 10s join → on timeout set _watchdog_thread = None → return (no close, no respawn) → launchd restarts the whole daemon. The 'safe recovery' framing of v2's path was a defense-in-depth that has not paid out — instead it kills v2 every ~1 hour with no observed SIGSEV mitigation value, because v1's pattern is observably safe on the same version of PyAV.
shipping_definition: (a) _scheduled_reconnect_fire proceeds with close + respawn on join timeout (matching v1-refactor semantics). (b) The 2026-09-08 'SIGSEGV aborted / launchd restart' rationale and code path are removed entirely from frame_capture.py — no `if old_thread.is_alive(): return` early-exit, no `self._watchdog_thread = None` abort. (c) The 2 watchdog-aborts tests in tests/test_rtsp_watchdog.py are rewritten to assert proceed-anyway behavior (close called even when join timed out, fresh decode thread spawned, _watchdog_thread NOT cleared). The happy-path test stays. (d) The test class is renamed from TestWatchdogAbortsOnZombieDecodeThread to TestWatchdogProceedAnywayOnStuckDecodeThread. (e) The defensive SIGSEGV docstring on _scheduled_reconnect_fire is removed. (f) US-017d acceptance criteria in docs/PHASE-V2-017-PRD-rtsp-robustness-and-delivery.json US-017d entry are amended to reflect proceed-anyway semantics, with the 2026-09-14 v1 evidence cited. (g) After merge to main, the v2 listener is restarted via launchd (operator-toggled per skill) and verified not to self-kill on the next scheduled_reconnect firing.
scope_exclusions: Do NOT touch _run_loop, _decode_iteration, _sleep_until_stop_or_watchdog, or the Phase 6B.155 cap-and-defer logic — those are the working parts of US-017e and stay unchanged.
Do NOT change scheduled_reconnect_seconds default (still 3600 = 1 hour).
Do NOT change watchdog 10s join timeout — the v1 path uses the same bound.

Do NOT add a new 'fallback' path or alternative handler — proceed-anyway IS the new handler. If the new path turns out to misbehave, ship US-039d (we have more cards now), don't reintroduce an `if join_times_out: abort` branch.
Do NOT modify listener/daemon.py, telegram_formatter, or any module outside infra/frame_capture.py and tests/test_rtsp_watchdog.py + the US-017d PRD JSON.
Do NOT bump v2 release version. This PRD lands on main as a code-only change.
design_principles: Mirror v1-refactor's behavior (persistent_rtsp.py _scheduled_reconnect_fire) — that is the proven, 456-fires-deep pattern. Don't invent new architecture.

No residue: when the abort path is removed, the SIGSEGV rationale comment, the 'Aborting reconnect' log string, and the early-return guard are ALL gone. No 'commented for posterity' / 'kept in case we need to revert'.

Test the observed behavior, not a hypothetical failure mode. The 2 abort tests were encoding a theory of what happens when join times out; reality (v1) is join does not time out and we proceed anyway. The new tests encode the proceed-anyway path + verify the stale path is gone.

stories.title: Port v1 proceed-anyway semantics: rewrite _scheduled_reconnect_fire + remove SIGSEVG rationale
stories.description:
**Story (PHASE-V2-039 / US-039a).** Port v1-refactor's proceed-anyway behavior to v2's _scheduled_reconnect_fire and remove the abort/SIGSEGV path entirely.

**PRD:** docs/PHASE-V2-039-PRD-rtsp-watchdog-proceed-anyway.json. **Type:** code. **Assignee:** coder. **Depends:** (none — first card in sweep).

**File in scope:** `infra/frame_capture.py` (method `_scheduled_reconnect_fire`, current lines 384-448).

**Behavior change:** the early-return `if old_thread.is_alive(): log.warning(... 'Aborting reconnect ...'); self._watchdog_thread = None; return` block (current lines 416-422) is GONE. Replaced by: log a 'Proceeding with reconnect anyway' warning, fall through to the container.close() + respawn block (which already handles close with try/except and clears _stop_event + spawns fresh decode thread + advances reconnects_total). The decorator/docstring on the method is also updated to cite v1's pattern and the 2026-09-14 evidence (456 fires, 0 SIGSEVG, 0 join-timeouts on the same PyAV 18.1.0).

**Defensive comment removal:** the explanatory comment block at current lines 401-408 that references SIGSEVG (offset 0x20 deref in *.ips crash dumps, launchd-restart-is-the-only-safe-recovery) is removed. v1 has 0 SIGSEVG over its lifetime; the comment is wrong by observation.

## Acceptance (8 ACs — each re-runnable)

- AC1: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'Aborting reconnect' -- infra/frame_capture.py | wc -l → 0 (no 'Aborting reconnect' string in frame_capture.py after port)
- AC2: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'SIGSEGV|launchd restart|left orphaned|AVFormatContext' -- infra/frame_capture.py | wc -l → 0 (no SIGSEGV-launchd-restart rationale in frame_capture.py)
- AC3: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'PyAV/FFmpeg will SIGSEGV' -- infra/frame_capture.py | wc -l → 0 (the specific comment phrasing is gone)
- AC4: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'self._watchdog_thread = None' -- infra/frame_capture.py | wc -l → 1 (only the line in stop() at L261 remains; abort path's self._watchdog_thread=None is gone)
- AC5: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'Proceeding with reconnect anyway' -- infra/frame_capture.py | wc -l → 1 (new log message is present)
- AC6: cd /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 && .venv/bin/python -c 'import infra.frame_capture; r = infra.frame_capture.PersistentRTSPReader("rtsp://u@127.0.0.1/x"); import inspect; src = inspect.getsource(r._scheduled_reconnect_fire); assert "Aborting reconnect" not in src and "Proceeding with reconnect anyway" in src; print("OK")' → exit 0
- AC7: cd /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_rtsp_watchdog.py::TestScheduledReconnectWatchdog -v --no-header 2>&1 | tail -10 → 1 passed (happy-path test still passes after proceed-anyway port)
- AC8: cd /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 && git diff main..HEAD -- infra/frame_capture.py | grep -cE '^[+-]' | awk '$1 > 0' → 1 (exactly one file changed in this story's branch)

stories.title: Amend US-017d acceptance criteria in PHASE-V2-017 PRD JSON to match proceed-anyway behavior
stories.description:
**Story (PHASE-V2-039 / US-039c).** Update the US-017d acceptance criteria in the existing PHASE-V2-017 PRD JSON so the spec matches the new (now-correct) behavior. Cite the 2026-09-14 evidence and the v1 reference.

**PRD:** docs/PHASE-V2-039-PRD-rtsp-watchdog-proceed-anyway.json. **Type:** docs. **Assignee:** coder. **Depends:** US-039a (the code must land first so the docs reflect reality), US-039b (test file docstring context is part of the same story as the tests).

**File in scope:** `docs/PHASE-V2-017-PRD-rtsp-robustness-and-delivery.json` (US-017d entry). Single story, single file. PRD JSON shape should be preserved (same `prd_id`, `stories` key, schema). Only the US-017d `title`/`description`/`acceptanceCriteria` fields get updated.

**Concrete changes:** US-017d acceptance criteria currently read: 'Proactive close+respawn every N seconds. Bounded 10s join on decode thread. If join times out → abort and let launchd restart.' Replace with: 'Proactive close+respawn every N seconds. Bounded 10s join on decode thread. If join times out, proceed with reconnect anyway: close _container (try/except) + spawn fresh decode thread alongside the stuck one. This matches v1-refactor's persistent_rtsp.py _scheduled_reconnect_fire pattern, which has run 456 fires on the same PyAV 18.1.0 / same cameras with 0 SIGSEVG and 0 join-timeouts (verified 2026-09-14 against rotated listener.log + listener.log.1). The 2026-09-08 abort-and-restart-launchd path was a defensive over-correction and is removed by PHASE-V2-039 / US-039a.' Also update the US-017d `rationale` field (or wherever the SIGSEVG-offset-0x20 line lives in this PRD) to cite the v1 evidence and note the corrective amendment.

## Acceptance (6 ACs — each re-runnable)

- AC1: git -C /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 grep -nE 'abort and let launchd restart' -- docs/PHASE-V2-017-PRD-rtsp-robustness-and-delivery.json | wc -l → 0 (old US-017d AC wording gone)
